finding: SSD/scan measured 114449.4ms, 99.661% of Mamba2 wall, 97.523% of total long prefill.
implication: GQA/HQQ attention and MoE/Marlin are not the next optimization target for this symptom.

finding: Dimensions are derived from config at runtime: d_inner, n_heads, head_dim, d_state, n_groups, chunk_size, bc_size, conv_dim, in_proj_dim.
implication: No Nano-specific hardcode is needed for analysis or a future fix.

finding: In-proj uses prefill_weight_gemm; split/extract is one CUDA kernel over row-major in_proj output.
implication: These substages measured 213.9ms and 18.5ms; not primary.

finding: Conv1d+silu launches mamba2_xbc_conv1d_silu_split plus a conv-state update kernel.
SSD launch computes threads from head_dim and launches one kernel per Mamba2 layer.
implication: Nano uses head_dim 64, threads 64, blocks_d 1, grid n_heads x blocks_d = 64 CTAs.

finding: The trace SSD kernel is used only when prefill-device trace has selected rows/dims; timing/liveness diagnostics use the normal mamba2_ssd kernel.
implication: The 1908 long diagnostic bottleneck is not caused by trace-kernel fallback.

finding: The normal SSD function handle is loaded from compiled PTX as mamba2_ssd_sequential_kernel.
implication: Hot path is Rust-launched CUDA, not Torch/Python.

finding: The C shim documents the intended chunked SSD algorithm: chunk size, parallel scan within chunks, sequential state passing between chunks.
implication: This describes the desired algorithmic direction but is not what the current Rust path launches.

finding: Kernel comment states the current implementation is a simple sequential scan equivalent to running decode N times; chunk-parallel version comes later.
implication: This is the source-level root cause of slow full prefill.

finding: Per-chunk dA prefix scan is built in shared memory per CTA.
implication: This part is not enough to make the whole kernel chunk-parallel because the main scan remains sequential over L and local u.

finding: Kernel loops sequentially over every token t from 0 to L.
implication: Runtime scales directly with prompt length inside each CTA.

finding: For each valid d, every t updates 128-state recurrent state.
implication: This is expected recurrent work but is only a small part compared with the local chunk scan.

finding: For each valid d and each t, kernel loops u from chunk_start to t.
implication: For chunk size 128 this averages 64.5 local u terms per token.

finding: Each local u term recomputes C[t] dot B[u] over state_size.
implication: CB depends on head/group/t/u, not head_dim d, so it is redundantly recomputed across all 64 d lanes.

finding: For chunks after the first, each local u term recomputes another C/B loop for old_state_source.
implication: This is another scalar term independent of d and duplicated across all 64 d lanes.

finding: Timing finish records CUDA event elapsed time and stream-sync time.
implication: In 1908 SSD wall/event/sync were all about 114.45s, so queueing or CPU-side wait is not the primary explanation.

finding: SSD input/output are row-major [L, n_heads, head_dim]; B/C are [L, n_groups, state_size].
implication: Layout is contiguous for the launched kernel; the issue is algorithmic duplicate scalar work, not an obvious non-contiguous transfer path.
